claims.claim: HTML provides six heading elements, h1 through h6, for headings.
The p element represents a paragraph and has phrasing content as its content model.
Heading information can be used by user agents to construct a document table of contents, and MDN advises authors not to skip heading levels.
W3C WAI states that headings communicate content organization and can support in-page navigation in browsers, plug-ins, and assistive technologies.
The HTML Standard says that a p element should not be used when a more specific element is appropriate and that lists cannot be children of p elements.
Visual treatment can vary independently of paragraph semantics, so CSS rather than heading rank should determine desired appearance.
